limits_note: Koyeb's startup programme advertises 'up to $30k in credits', which is a separate application, not a signup grant.
reliability_note: scale-to-zero is silent from the client's side, a request after an hour pays a cold start instead of an error; the pricing page carries the banner 'Koyeb is joining Mistral AI to Build The Future of AI Infrastructure', which puts the free tier's longevity in question
notes: The corpus record carried identity kind 'email' with 'no card for the free Instance'. The pricing FAQ read says the opposite, in a section titled 'Why does Koyeb require a credit card?'. The Scale-to-Zero documentation states the feature is 'currently in public preview', which is a second reason not to build a 03:00 job on it without a watchdog. The USD 29 hold, the prorated charge and the debit acceptance are all confirmed verbatim on the vendor's pricing FAQ. This is the largest published hold of the seventeen vendors checked, and it is on the free tier.

free_tier.stated: One Free Instance per organization: 512 MB of RAM, 0.1 vCPU, 2 GB of SSD, in Frankfurt or Washington D.C. only; not usable as a Worker Service, no custom scaling, no volumes.

retention.stated: no persistent storage: 'They can't be used with Volumes to add persistent storage to your services'

egress.terms: 100 GB of outbound bandwidth a month free, then USD 0.04 per GB; the vendor says outbound bandwidth is not charged yet and will be announced before it is

identity_cost.detail: card required even for the free Instance; USD 29 pre-authorisation hold, released immediately or within 7 to 21 days depending on the issuer; a prorated Pro charge is taken at the same moment; debit accepted; prepaid is not stated

evidence.proved: one free web Service with 512 MB RAM, 0.1 vCPU and 2 GB SSD; one free PostgreSQL database with 5 hours of active time
